method_card.title: School Subjects and the School Day
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school subject vocabulary, telling the time in German, and giving reasoned opinions about your timetable using weil and obwohl.

GermanEnglish
die Mathematik / Mathemaths
die Naturwissenschaftscience
die Geschichtehistory
die Erdkundegeography
die Kunstart
der SportPE
die InformatikIT/computing
die Fremdspracheforeign language
Mein Lieblingsfachmy favourite subject
interessantinteresting
langweiligboring
nützlichuseful
schwer / schwierigdifficult
Es macht Spaß.It is fun.
die Note, -ngrade / mark

Grammar focus 1 — opinions with finden and weil: Say Ich finde + subject + adjective to give an opinion: Ich finde Mathe schwer. Add a reason with weil: after weil, the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause. Example: Mein Lieblingsfach ist Musik, weil es Spaß macht.

Grammar focus 2 — telling the time: German uses a different logic from English. Halb means 'half to' the next hour, NOT 'half past'. So halb neun = 8:30 (half to nine). Viertel vor sieben = 6:45. Viertel nach sieben = 7:15. Drill these carefully — they are opposite to English intuition.
Time phrases force inversion: Montags habe ich Englisch. (verb second, subject after).

Model paragraph: Mein Lieblingsfach ist Musik, weil es kreativ und interessant ist. Ich finde Mathe schwer, obwohl ich gute Noten bekomme. Montags in der ersten Stunde habe ich Deutsch um Viertel nach acht.
(My favourite subject is Music because it is creative and interesting. I find Maths difficult, although I get good grades. On Mondays in the first period I have German at quarter past eight.)

method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school facilities, rules using modal verbs, uniform descriptions with accusative adjective endings, and school issues such as stress and bullying.

GermanEnglish
das Klassenzimmerclassroom
die Kantinecanteen
die Bibliotheklibrary
die Turnhallegymnasium
der Schulhofschool yard
man mussyou must / one must
man darf nichtyou must not / one is not allowed to
man sollyou should / one should
die Schuluniformschool uniform
tragento wear
das Mobbingbullying
der Stressstress
der Prüfungsdruckexam pressure
Ich denke, dass...I think that...
hässlich / praktischugly / practical

Grammar focus 1 — modal verbs for rules: Man muss / soll / darf nicht + infinitive at end. The modal sits at position 2; the infinitive goes to the clause end. Example: Man muss die Schuluniform tragen. Never put the infinitive immediately after the modal as in English ('Man muss tragen die Uniform' is wrong).

Grammar focus 2 — accusative adjective endings after uniform: Tragen (to wear) takes the accusative case. After einen/eine/ein, adjective endings are: masculine -en (einen roten Rock), feminine -e (eine blaue Hose), neuter -es (ein weißes Hemd), plural -e (schwarze Schuhe).

Grammar focus 3 — dass clauses: Like weil and obwohl, the conjunction dass sends the verb to the end: Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform bequem ist.

Model paragraph: In meiner Schule gibt es eine Kantine und eine große Bibliothek. Man muss die Schuluniform tragen. Ich trage eine blaue Jacke, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe. Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform praktisch ist, obwohl sie manchmal unbequem ist.
(In my school there is a canteen and a large library. You must wear school uniform. I wear a blue blazer, a white shirt and black shoes. I think that school uniform is practical, although it is sometimes uncomfortable.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school rules and uniform appear regularly in 50-word writing tasks and speaking conversations

method_card.title: Jobs and Work Experience
method_card.content:
This lesson covers jobs vocabulary, the German feminine suffix -in, work experience, and giving opinions about future careers. It is built fresh from the German specification — there is no direct parallel in other board courses.

GermanEnglish
der Arzt / die Ärztindoctor (m/f)
der Lehrer / die Lehrerinteacher (m/f)
der Krankenpfleger / die Krankenschwesternurse (m/f)
der Ingenieur / die Ingenieurinengineer (m/f)
der Rechtsanwalt / die Rechtsanwältinlawyer (m/f)
der Koch / die Köchincook/chef (m/f)
der Verkäufer / die Verkäuferinshop assistant (m/f)
der Beruf, die Berufeprofession / job
das Praktikumwork experience / internship
die Firmacompany / firm
arbeitento work
Ich möchte ... werden.I would like to become ...

Grammar focus 1 — profession as predicate: NO article: In German, you do not use an article before a profession when it follows sein (to be) as a predicate. Say Ich bin Lehrer (I am a teacher), NOT Ich bin ein Lehrer. However, if you add an adjective, the article returns: Ich bin ein guter Lehrer.

Grammar focus 2 — feminine forms with -in: Most male job titles become feminine by adding -in: der Lehrer → die Lehrerin, der Arzt → die Ärztin (with umlaut), der Koch → die Köchin (with umlaut). This suffix is a key feature of German and must be used correctly when referring to women.

Grammar focus 3 — future with möchte/will/werden: Three ways to express future plans: (1) Ich möchte Ärztin werden (I would like to become a doctor — modal + infinitive at end); (2) Ich werde Ingenieur (I will be an engineer — werden present = future); (3) present tense + future adverb: Nächstes Jahr mache ich ein Praktikum.

Model paragraph: Ich möchte in der Zukunft Ärztin werden, weil ich Menschen helfen möchte. Letzten Sommer habe ich ein Praktikum bei einer Firma gemacht. Ich fand es interessant, obwohl es manchmal stressig war.
(I would like to become a doctor in the future because I would like to help people. Last summer I did work experience at a company. I found it interesting, although it was sometimes stressful.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — future plans and work experience appear in writing tasks and speaking conversations about future opportunities

method_card.title: Future Plans and Career Aspirations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers post-16 plans, university and career aspirations using three future structures and Konjunktiv II. The German post-16 education system differs significantly from the UK system — key terms are culturally specific and must be learned accurately.

GermanEnglish
das AbiturGerman school-leaving certificate (≈ A-levels)
die Ausbildungapprenticeship / vocational training
das Studiumuniversity studies / degree course
die Universität (Uni)university
die Fachhochschule (FH)university of applied sciences (≈ polytechnic)
das Praktikumwork experience / internship
der Berufjob / profession
in der Zukunftin the future
nach der Schuleafter school
ich werde ... werdenI will become ...
ich würde gernI would like to (conditional)
ich möchteI would like (polite modal)

Grammar focus 1 — three future structures (all must appear in your writing):

(1) Present tense + future adverb: Nächstes Jahr mache ich ein Praktikum. (Next year I am doing work experience.) Simple, natural, frequently used in spoken German.

(2) Werden + infinitive (formal future): Modal-style structure — werden at position 2, infinitive at the clause end. Ich werde Informatik studieren. (I will study computer science.) In a subordinate clause, both verbs go to the end: weil ich Informatik studieren werde.

(3) Modal + infinitive at end: Ich möchte auf die Universität gehen. or Ich will eine Ausbildung machen.

Grammar focus 2 — Konjunktiv II for aspirations and advice: Use ich würde gern + infinitive for 'I would like to': Ich würde gern Medizin studieren. Use man sollte + infinitive for advice: Man sollte gute Noten bekommen. Use es wäre + adjective for 'it would be': Es wäre toll, wenn ich das Abitur bestehe.

Model paragraph: Nach der Schule möchte ich das Abitur machen und dann werde ich auf die Universität gehen. Ich würde gern Medizin studieren, weil ich Ärztin werden möchte. Ich denke, dass eine Ausbildung auch eine gute Option wäre.
(After school I would like to do my Abitur and then I will go to university. I would like to study Medicine because I would like to become a doctor. I think that an apprenticeship would also be a good option.)

exam_context.frequency: Higher-yield topic for writing and speaking — future tense and Konjunktiv II are required for top marks

gold.source_text: After school I will go to university and study Medicine. I would like to become a doctor because I find it interesting to help people. I think that an apprenticeship would also be a good option.
model_answers: Nach der Schule werde ich auf die Universität gehen und Medizin studieren. Ich möchte Ärztin werden, weil ich es interessant finde, Menschen zu helfen. Ich denke, dass eine Ausbildung auch eine gute Option wäre.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich möchte auf die Universität gehen.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Werden is conjugated and goes at position 2 in a main clause: Ich werde Informatik studieren.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The main verb (infinitive) goes to the end of the main clause — just like a modal verb.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: In a subordinate clause (after weil, dass, obwohl), both verbs go to the end, conjugated form last: weil ich Informatik studieren werde.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Main clause: Subject + werde + … + infinitive. Subordinate: … + infinitive + werde.

worked_examples.question: Explain the word order rule with werden + infinitive.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich möchte auf die Uni gehen uses the modal möchte — it expresses a wish or preference (I would like to go). It is polite and tentative.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Ich werde auf die Uni gehen uses werden + infinitive — it states a definite plan or fact about the future (I will go).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Use möchte for wishes and preferences; use werden + infinitive for firm future plans. Both have the infinitive at the clause end.

worked_examples.question: What is the difference between 'ich möchte ... gehen' and 'ich werde ... gehen'?

ai_marking_prompts.writing: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about future plans and career aspirations. Mark on: Communication (post-school plan, university vs apprenticeship comparison, career aspiration, advice), Range of language (all three future structures, Konjunktiv II forms, discourse markers einerseits/andererseits/jedoch, weil/dass/obwohl + verb-final, comparatives), Accuracy (werden + infinitive at end including in subordinate clauses, Konjunktiv II: wäre/hätte/würde/sollte, profession without article after sein/werden, verb-final in subordinate clauses, noun capitalisation, umlauts including Universität, Ausbildung). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}
ai_marking_prompts.role_play: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a role play about future plans and career aspirations. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: werden + infinitive at end (both verbs to end in subordinate clauses), möchte/würde gern + infinitive at end, Konjunktiv II (wäre, sollte), weil/dass + verb-final, Sie register in formal transactional settings (leisure centre, hotel, etc.), noun capitalisation. Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}
ai_marking_prompts.translate_to_target: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a translation from English to German. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Accept any grammatically correct translation that conveys the same meaning. Check: all three future structures (present + adverb, werden + infinitive at end, möchte/will + infinitive at end), Konjunktiv II (würde gern, wäre, hätte, sollte), verb-final in subordinate clauses after weil/dass/obwohl, profession after werden/sein has no article, noun capitalisation and umlauts. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}
